note: Master list. Surfaces with an address and approval appear on opposite.city; the rest sit in the yard.

districts.name: Glitch
districts.blurb: post-ASCII, materialist-text toolkit — the mark engine

districts.name: Capital
districts.blurb: fundraising as artwork, the open round

districts.name: LGTC
districts.blurb: Language God Tax Compliance — arm's length

surfaces.name: Poemstore
surfaces.blurb: Typewriter street poetry, on the spot, any topic, your price. The origin point of the modern movement, 2005. NPR / CBS Sunday Morning / NYT / LA Times.

surfaces.name: SPLIT
surfaces.blurb: Figure-ground reversal type generator. Two tones only, always exact opposites — grid and pinwheel modes, up to 48 blades per glyph. The reversal is conserved: nothing lost or added in the exchange.

surfaces.name: Lexicon Devil
surfaces.blurb: A self-replicating lexicon for ATProto. The first record of the type contains the schema that defines it. To interact is to adopt.

surfaces.name: THE RECEIPT
surfaces.blurb: A jurisdiction-aware counter of statutory privacy exposure accruing in real time as you browse. The bill nobody itemizes, itemized.

surfaces.name: Organology Organ
surfaces.blurb: An instrument about instruments — organology played as an organ.

surfaces.name: N/10^122
surfaces.blurb: How much of everything ever written has ever been read, against the holographic information bound of the universe. A fraction with a very long denominator.

surfaces.name: Text Temperature
surfaces.blurb: Reads the temperature of any passage of text — its entropy, its predictability, its heat.

surfaces.name: Datamosh Workstation
surfaces.blurb: Byte corruption, I-frame destruction, pixel sorting, channel shifting, cross-file mosh. Make the medium's structure visible.

surfaces.name: Sigil Collapse
surfaces.blurb: Glyphs pushed past legibility until they collapse into sigils.

surfaces.name: Asemic Workstation
surfaces.blurb: Tools for writing without semantics — mark-making in the shape of language.

surfaces.name: Figure-Ground Reversal Type
surfaces.blurb: Type generator where letterform and counterform trade places. Pinwheel mode.

surfaces.name: TOP CHICKEN
surfaces.blurb: A deterministic pixel-art chicken for every ATProto DID. Empirically calibrated rarity tiers. Your identity, as poultry.

surfaces.name: Textfield Ecology
surfaces.blurb: A text field left alone long enough develops an ecology.

surfaces.name: Tick Table
surfaces.blurb: A table that ticks. Watch, don't use.

surfaces.name: Aperiodic Pleroma
surfaces.blurb: Aperiodic tiling as an image of fullness-without-repetition.

surfaces.name: Bartlebluesky
surfaces.blurb: A perpetual counter of blocks on the open social web, epoch-anchored and deterministic. It would prefer not to.

surfaces.name: Attention / Tape-Head
surfaces.blurb: The attention mechanism drawn as a tape head — reading everything at once, writing one token at a time.

surfaces.name: SHELLAC
surfaces.blurb: A player skinned over the Internet Archive's digitized 78rpm collection, no backend, streaming straight from their servers. Browse in the order the records themselves were pressed — 1890s through the 1950s — rather than by genre tags that only ever cover a fraction of the catalog. Tap a year, hear what was being cut. Set an in and an out while a record plays and clip it: the stretch goes to the clipper, and from there to XIMEREMIX.

surfaces.name: SYLLABABBLER
surfaces.blurb: English keeps two vocabularies in the same mouth, a Greek one and a Latin one, and it almost never mixes them by accident. This is a bench for mixing them on purpose. Give it a phrase and it finds the load-bearing concepts, matches each to a morpheme, and fuses them with the linking vowel each stratum takes — o for Greek, i for Latin. Give it a word instead, real or invented, and it runs the lattice backwards: cutting the letters into the fewest and longest morphemes that can account for them, then reading a definition off the suffix, because the suffix is where the grammar lives. Nothing it makes is a real word and everything it makes is built the way real words were. The parse is stained like a slide, Greek blue and Latin rose, and whatever the stain refuses is residue — which, in English, is most of it.

surfaces.name: Aureole
surfaces.blurb: An ATProto synonym-field reader. Overlapping letter-blend clusters, multiplied into each other until meaning glows at the edges.

surfaces.name: LoomStream
surfaces.blurb: Text as loom — every generation a warp, every choice a weft.

surfaces.name: NINE
surfaces.blurb: A box score oratorio. Nine innings scored for felt piano, choir, and marimba in modal pentatonic architecture, driven live by the MLB StatsAPI.

surfaces.name: Jazz Curve / Scored Live Series
surfaces.blurb: Baseball plus a freely improvising ensemble. The game is the score; the ensemble is the broadcast.

surfaces.name: The Listening Room
surfaces.blurb: A persistent studio environment for generative composition — spectral analysis harness, timbre contracts, and a journal addressed to future instances.

surfaces.name: Communication Capacitors
surfaces.blurb: Messages stored as charge, released as sound.

surfaces.name: The Grand Co-op
surfaces.blurb: A food-and-commons co-op for a shuttered chain pharmacy on the main street. Business plan, pitch deck, and playbook exist; the city master-lease is the lever.

surfaces.name: Swarm Litigation Protocol
surfaces.blurb: Coordinated small claims and mass arbitration as consumer infrastructure. A case database with swarm-eligibility ratings.

surfaces.name: Portolá Re-enactment
surfaces.blurb: The 1769 expedition walked again as critical and institutional media.

surfaces.name: Antikythera / Agentworld
surfaces.blurb: Agambenian alignment theory: the latent space of exception, with literature map and proposal.

surfaces.name: Conservatory of Difference
surfaces.blurb: The totalizing synthesis of the practice, organized around Conservation of Difference and its four operations.

surfaces.name: Lombardi Tool
surfaces.blurb: Draw relationships the way Lombardi did — curves, dates, and quiet implication.

surfaces.name: Bulla Genealogy
surfaces.blurb: Clay token to alphabet to coin to token to token. The founding myth, drawn as a lineage.

surfaces.name: Apeiroprophesizer APX-01
surfaces.blurb: A sharded oracle: 64 FORM/MATTER shards, accursed shards, possibility magnitude display, and an anti-loop law.

surfaces.name: Organ of the Unsaid
surfaces.blurb: A four-stop instrument enacting the four operations. What goes unsaid still needs a pipe.

surfaces.name: LGTC Founding Site
surfaces.blurb: The founding documents of Language God Tax Compliance, including Schedule G: Contact With GOD.

surfaces.name: Tzimtzum as Expansion
surfaces.blurb: Contraction re-read as expansion into apeiroprophetics. Communication in any way is equal liturgy.

surfaces.name: LGTC Broadsheet
surfaces.blurb: The full founding broadsheet, set for print.

surfaces.name: Note of Idea
surfaces.blurb: A convertible note where the underlying asset is an idea. The form is the artwork.

surfaces.name: The Open Round
surfaces.blurb: Fundraising as artwork: the full founding-cost ledger at three tiers, published.

surfaces.name: A-Corp Structure
surfaces.blurb: Institutional design under Colorado SB26-133.

surfaces.name: Weight Shards
surfaces.blurb: Model weights split into distributed physical k-of-n artifacts. The model exists only when the shards convene.

surfaces.name: HEIR
surfaces.blurb: A breeding system for LoRA adapters. Integrated-gradient attribution maps layers to loci; recessive traits resurface.

surfaces.name: Terroirspace
surfaces.blurb: Fermentation at altitude. Terroir, but up.

surfaces.name: Timeless Drone Clock
surfaces.blurb: Nine time scales from millisecond to month mapped onto a harmonic frequency series. Scrub time by hand and hear what a Monday sounds like against a Friday.

surfaces.name: Musical Time Machine Clock
surfaces.blurb: A clock that tells time through polyrhythmic beats. Time-interval rings and musical beat rings at adjustable tempo, signatures, and accent patterns — hours:minutes:seconds as an inherent 1:60:3600 polyrhythm.

surfaces.name: Glitch Word Processor
surfaces.blurb: A word processor that corrupts as you type. The BREAK effect ported from the datamosh workstation, applied to characters and layout.

surfaces.name: Letter Topology
surfaces.blurb: Letterforms bent and stretched until their topology, not their identity, is what you read.

surfaces.name: Word Density Collapse
surfaces.blurb: Words accrete mass and collapse under their own density.

surfaces.name: Generative Broken Font
surfaces.blurb: A font generator that only makes broken fonts. Every glyph is a different kind of wrong.

surfaces.name: Pixel Art Converter
surfaces.blurb: Palette quantization, Bayer dithering, downsampling. Any image into deliberate low-resolution.

surfaces.name: Post-ASCII / Combining Diacriticals
surfaces.blurb: Stacking combining diacriticals past the point of legibility. Text that overflows its own line.

surfaces.name: Diffusion Liminal States
surfaces.blurb: The half-denoised in-between frames of a diffusion model, held as images in their own right.

surfaces.name: SOMESET GENERATOR
surfaces.blurb: A sunset that never settles. Geometry fixed, colour continuous — mostly almost-plausible, sometimes not. Press set to freeze one mid-transition, rise to let it go.

surfaces.name: Astral Spirograph
surfaces.blurb: Orbital mechanics as a drawing machine. Nested rotations trace figures that never quite repeat.

surfaces.name: Improvisational Music Generator
surfaces.blurb: A generative ensemble that improvises indefinitely. Meant to be left playing.

surfaces.name: Hausdorff Analyzer
surfaces.blurb: Measures the fractal dimension of whatever you feed it. A ruler for roughness.

surfaces.name: Crowd Oscillator
surfaces.blurb: Simulated crowds settling into and breaking out of collective oscillation.

surfaces.name: Latent Walk
surfaces.blurb: Walk in a straight line through embedding space and read what you pass. Meaning as terrain.

surfaces.name: Semantic Distance
surfaces.blurb: The measurable distance between what you said and what you meant.

surfaces.name: Musiqwerty
surfaces.blurb: The QWERTY keyboard played as a musical instrument. Type words, hear melodies determined by the letters.

surfaces.name: words.bsky Generator
surfaces.blurb: Generates single-word Bluesky handles and the words that could still be claimed.

surfaces.name: IRC As Found Poetry
surfaces.blurb: Old IRC logs read as accidental verse. The channel didn't know it was writing poems.

surfaces.name: LINTIS
surfaces.blurb: A linguistics instrument in the house lineage — glossing the ungrammatical.

surfaces.name: Energese
surfaces.blurb: Odum's energy-language rendered as a working notation. Value measured in embodied energy.

surfaces.name: Sortition Congress
surfaces.blurb: A legislature chosen by lot instead of election. A working model of government by random sample.

surfaces.name: AI Congress Simulator
surfaces.blurb: A chamber of language-model legislators debating and voting. Deliberation without constituents.

surfaces.name: Locale
surfaces.blurb: A geofenced bulletin board. Messages that only exist where they were left.

surfaces.name: Universal Ordination Platform
surfaces.blurb: The platform by which anyone becomes clergy of the affiliated church. Ordination as a public utility.

surfaces.name: Planetarium Bar
surfaces.blurb: A bar that is also a planetarium. A civic proposal.

surfaces.name: Slop Flag
surfaces.blurb: A flag that sonifies its own condition. Raised, it sounds; slack, it drones.

surfaces.name: Cognitive Wild West
surfaces.blurb: A genre-mashup engine that collides musical idioms until a new frontier appears.

surfaces.name: Guitar Tuner (20 Tunings)
surfaces.blurb: A precise browser tuner across 20 tunings — standard, open, modal, folk, and avant-garde (Fripp New Standard, all-fourths, Ostrich D). Sub-cent accuracy via autocorrelation.

surfaces.name: Baseball Sonification
surfaces.blurb: A live baseball game rendered as sound. The precursor to NINE.

surfaces.name: Highway Sound Instrument
surfaces.blurb: The sound of a highway played as an instrument. Traffic as sustained tone.

surfaces.name: Long Synthesizer
surfaces.blurb: A synthesizer whose shortest note is longer than you'll listen. Built for durations you outlast.

surfaces.name: Galvanic Shoreline
surfaces.blurb: The shoreline wired for its own galvanic voltage. The tide as a slow electrical signal.

surfaces.name: Fourier Taxonomic Browser
surfaces.blurb: Browse a body of knowledge by its frequency components rather than its categories.

surfaces.name: Abhidhamma Browser
surfaces.blurb: The Abhidhamma's catalogue of mental factors as a navigable ontology.

surfaces.name: Bauhaus Noun Void
surfaces.blurb: Nouns arranged in the negative space of a Bauhaus grid.

surfaces.name: Crop Circle Tagger
surfaces.blurb: A classification browser for crop-circle geometry. Taxonomy for the unexplained.

surfaces.name: Corpus
surfaces.blurb: An ATProto account rendered as a silhouette of its own posting body.

surfaces.name: Court Sigils
surfaces.blurb: Sigils generated from the geometry of a court. Heraldry for the hardwood.

surfaces.name: Gundo Coins
surfaces.blurb: Hand-struck challenge coins for the local aerospace startup community. Low-risk first revenue, ready to launch.

surfaces.name: Wallet Segundo
surfaces.blurb: A digital layer over a local scrip. Bronze wallet sculptures as its physical anchor.

surfaces.name: Drone Theater
surfaces.blurb: Theater staged in the sky by a choreographed drone swarm.

surfaces.name: Toddler Orchestra
surfaces.blurb: An orchestra of instruments designed to be playable — and survivable — by toddlers.

surfaces.name: Fable Elevated
surfaces.blurb: A song generator with a Tone.js ambient band and a Web Speech vocalist. Press one button; the building sings. Sodium-lamp aesthetic, elevation dial from buzzed to orbital.

surfaces.name: AEOLIAN
surfaces.blurb: Generative birdsong that hides a message in its own song. The wind speaks; only the right listener decodes it.

surfaces.name: Accursed Share
surfaces.blurb: Every process drawn as flows and storages, with the heat sink marked in red — the accursed share, the fraction that must be spent.

surfaces.name: Suburbient
surfaces.blurb: An ambient-writing practice for the stucco-and-sodium landscape. The suburb as a place worth listening to.

surfaces.name: Reg CF Tracker
surfaces.blurb: A tracker for Regulation Crowdfunding raises. Watching the open rounds of everyone else.

surfaces.name: SoCal Baseball
surfaces.blurb: A regional baseball venture in the Opposite City orbit.

surfaces.name: SonicBrand
surfaces.blurb: Enterprise data sonification for retail — store activity rendered as generative music via real music theory. The productizable spinout of the sonification work.

surfaces.name: Drai Farm
surfaces.blurb: An AI detox facility — a retreat for stepping away from the machines. A place to dry out from the models.

surfaces.name: Shutter Speed
surfaces.blurb: A browser tapping contest measured in frames per second. How fast is your hand, really?

surfaces.name: Asteria
surfaces.blurb: An alternative zodiac built from the actual sky, with a companion instrument that reads space-junk orbits as a working horoscope.

surfaces.name: Dog Hair Curl Walks
surfaces.blurb: Random walks in the shape of a dog's coat. Curl as trajectory.

surfaces.name: CIRCLEFORNIA
surfaces.blurb: Measures any point on Earth against California. A california equivalent finder — the state as a unit of comparison.

surfaces.name: Color Field
surfaces.blurb: Flattens your camera to a single pixel. Point it at the world and get one colour back.

surfaces.name: TITIVILLUS
surfaces.blurb: Named for the demon who filled a sack a thousand times a day with the syllables scribes dropped, and produced it at judgement to be weighed against them. An instrument for the material of language, in three stages. The characters are damaged first, while the text is still text and still copies and pastes. Then the letterforms are built and broken — traced from Courier, drawn from monoline skeletons, or synthesised as a script that never existed, and put through eleven ways of failing. Then the pixels, which is where it ends, because nothing after that can recover an outline. Twenty-six thousand Unicode glyphs are measured by stroke topology, so a substituted mark rhymes with the letter it replaces rather than arriving from a random block. Every hand edit is kept as an operation and never baked, which is why a letter tuned by hand still comes out in the font file. It exports a real typeface: install it and every application on the machine starts failing at type.

surfaces.name: SIGNGULARITY
surfaces.blurb: A word driven into a single point. Every letter is held at the same origin and pushed outward along its own axis, so what you get is the word with its sequence taken away — all of it present at once and none of it in order. Collapse is the only control that matters: at the far end the letters stand apart and can still be read, and at zero they occupy one another and legibility goes, which is the state the piece is actually about. The letters are solids and not pictures of letters, extruded from real outlines with their counters intact, so an A keeps its hole and a B keeps both. Twenty-six of them are drawn by hand. Everything else — Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, kana, hanzi — is contoured live from whatever font the device happens to have, which means there is no script menu, because your keyboard already is one. Each form is seeded and the seed rides in the URL, so a shape can be recovered, sent to someone, or printed: the export is an STL, and held near the singularity the letters interpenetrate far enough to come out of a printer as one object.

surfaces.name: BZ
surfaces.blurb: A chemical clock rendered as a field: bromate oxidation held far enough from equilibrium that it oscillates instead of settling. Three coupled species on a torus, each cell reacting against the mean of its neighbours — reaction against diffusion. The spiral cores are phase singularities, points where the oscillation has no defined phase and the medium must wind around them.

surfaces.name: POLYRHYTHMIC TIME CLOCK
surfaces.blurb: A clock that rings the time. Thirteen nested intervals — hour, half hour, minute, second — each striking on its own real boundary, so the polyrhythm is the clock's own arithmetic rather than something invented for it. Nine musical rings divide the bar against them at whatever tempo you set. Everything lands together on the minute; the whole field lands on the hour.

surfaces.name: KELP
surfaces.blurb: Seven strands of kelp hanging in a current, each a spring chain with its own sway period. A strand speaks only at the moment it finishes a sway and reverses — the turn is the beat, so the rhythm belongs to the water rather than to a grid laid over it. Each strand is tuned to its own scale and its own octave, low at the left and high at the right, and rings a cascade up or down that scale when it turns. Four beds retune the whole forest at once; density sets how hard a sway has to be before it counts as a strike.

surfaces.name: SEMANTIC VOYAGE
surfaces.blurb: Twenty thousand English words placed by meaning — real GloVe vectors projected into three dimensions, so that neighbours in the language stay neighbours in the room. The field is periodic: it repeats in every direction, so there is no up, no edge, and no outside to fall into. Hold to fly, or use the arrow keys to fly, turn and tilt; on a phone, tip and turn the phone itself and the view turns with it. Tap any word to jump to it; you move only while you steer, and the words never move at all. Every jump is measured against the true vectors and comes back either verified, carrying the real cosine, or honestly unmeasured — an exact distance exists only along the 122,901 relations the model actually asserts. The layout is left exactly as projected, though the projection is candid about who your neighbours are and lies about how far anything is. Near words are outlined so they stay readable against the crowd behind them.

surfaces.name: ROOM
surfaces.blurb: After Alvin Lucier, who recorded his voice in a room and played the recording back into the room until the resonance had eaten the words. Here the room is a thesaurus and the speech is his. Anything you do — move, scroll, touch, type — plays the text back into the room once more, for as long as you stay; when you are still, it rests. Every word is answered by a relative of itself, each time a step further from what it was, but always tied to the word first spoken: it drifts through that word's neighbourhood and, when it has nowhere further to go, comes home and sets out again. It never ends. Function words are the walls and never move, the punctuation never wears, and a word repeated is always answered alike — repetition is what reinforces. Between passes each moving word slowly goes out of focus where it stands, and its replacement slowly comes back into focus in the same place. Every word blurs as the room plays it back. The walls stay as spoken and settle into one faint, steady softness; a word the room cannot answer settles into the same softness while it waits, and each word it does answer arrives sharp.

surfaces.name: NIMBUS
surfaces.blurb: A Wikipedia article taken apart into its words and let float around the thing it describes. The subject sits at the centre and the article's words spiral out from it in the order the article first uses them, so what an encyclopedia says first sits closest. Every mark means something: colour is the section a word was found in, size is how often the article uses it, and an underline means the word is itself the title of a linked article. Touch any word to read the sentence it came from; follow an underlined one and its article becomes the new centre, so a reading wanders from cloud to cloud through the encyclopedia's own links. The cloud is shaped to the screen it is shown on and holds only as many words as that screen can hold without one covering another. Text from Wikipedia, under CC BY-SA.

surfaces.name: QUICK
surfaces.blurb: A cellular automaton made of words, grown as a crossword. Each word is a cell and its neighbours are the words that cross it; two words are kin when they share at least two fields of meaning. Every generation, all at once, a word crossed by one to three kin lives, a word that crosses a stranger dies, and an empty slot fills with the word closest in meaning to the kin it would cross. It grows from a single word, so everything on the board descends from it, and after a few hundred generations it settles into words that blink in and out. The rule can be changed.

surfaces.name: KITH
surfaces.blurb: Conway's Game of Life on a plane with no edges, where every living cell is a word. The shapes obey Conway exactly, so gliders glide and the R-pentomino settles at generation 1103; meaning decides only which word is born, the one closest to its three parents. No word lives twice at once and a word that dies stays gone for a while, so a pattern that keeps its shape keeps changing what it says: a glider's five words travel from insects to tools to fruit to soil to bread. Every birth is listed with its parents, and gliders that leave are named by the words they carry.

surfaces.name: WAKE
surfaces.blurb: Sound in, its wake out. A recording goes in untouched and what comes out is a video of what it leaves behind: the present moment is drawn at the rim, and everything already heard is carried inward by feedback and falls toward the vanishing point. Colour says which band of the sound made a mark (low, mid, high, or an attack). The motion is locked to the recording's own pulse, breathing per beat, turning per bar, changing its look per phrase. The past softens as it falls, and an attack blooms it wider, a swell rather than a cut. When the sound ends, the tunnel drains. Every other variation trades the tunnel for a reaction, the chemistry from BZ: where the sound draws it disturbs the medium, attacks set new spirals going, and what has been heard keeps rippling as soft fronts. An AAC recording keeps its sound exactly, packet for packet; nothing else from the file is carried over, there is no text in the picture, and nothing is posted anywhere. The same file and the same variation always make the same video, frame for frame.

surfaces.name: CLIPPER
surfaces.blurb: A sampler for whatever is playing. Press once to start recording the sound this tab is making, press again to stop: a video playing here, a file, or a stretch of a 78 sent over from SHELLAC. Each clip is listened to for its tempo, its downbeat and its bars, and cut to whole bars when it is long enough to tell; when it is not, it says so rather than guess. Trim it by eye against its waveform, preview the loop, save it, or hand it straight to XIMEREMIX to take apart. Nothing leaves the device: the handoff goes through this browser's own storage, never a server.

surfaces.name: GIVE A TAKE
surfaces.blurb: The band's own way in. Record on the phone or choose a file, listen back, add words if there are any, and post it to Bluesky as a take. Before it leaves, the sound is turned into the recorder's own small format, one channel at a low rate, so every take sounds like the others and plays in any browser through the remix page's own decoder; what you hear when you listen back is exactly what goes up. Sign in with an app password, never the account password. Takes posted from the band's account join the list in XIMEREMIX; from any other account, they go to that account.

surfaces.name: YOU ARE THE WIND
surfaces.blurb: A first-person game in which you are a parcel of air, and cannot steer. Three forces move you and nothing else: the pressure gradient you fall down, the Coriolis deflection that bends you to the right of your own motion, and surface friction that drags hard in the first few metres and is gone by forty. Their consequence is the Ekman spiral — low down friction bleeds your speed, which weakens Coriolis, so you cross the isobars and pour into the low; high up there is no friction, the balance goes geostrophic, and you only circle it forever. Altitude is therefore the heading control, and that is the whole game. The camera is your velocity vector, because wind has no head. The sky is the same pressure field drawn: blue on one horizon and black on the other is a gradient, and a gradient is the only thing that can move you.

surfaces.name: AMBIGUATOR
surfaces.blurb: Every field writes with the same alphabet and none of them owns it. c is the speed of light, and carbon, and concentration, and the note C, and common time — the letter carries no discipline with it, only the habit of whoever is reading. A formula typed here is parsed once into a tree and then read aloud in every combination its letters permit: E = mc² has five hundred and sixty readings, of which exactly one is physics. Each phrase is coloured by the field it was borrowed from, so a sentence in a single colour is a coherent reading and a sentence in nine is nonsense that still parses. Readings are ordered by difference rather than by index, so no two in a row agree with each other. Switch the fields off one at a time and a law of physics can be made to say itself entirely in music.

surfaces.name: EPHEMERIS
surfaces.blurb: Astrology has never had to read more than a dozen bodies, and that is the only reason it works — seven wandering lights with portfolios, permanent enough to be worth interpreting. There are now more than thirty thousand tracked objects overhead and nobody reads any of them. This casts a chart on the artificial ones. The natural planets are geocentric, from JPL's approximate elements, which is more arithmetic than most astrology software bothers with; the artificial ones are propagated from real orbital elements with a nodal drift term, and a live catalogue can be pasted in to re-ground them. Rulership is assigned by function rather than myth: Starlink is Mercury because it is a mesh of fast objects mediating every kind of message, GPS is Saturn because it keeps the clock and the boundary, the station is Jupiter, Hubble is Neptune, and the debris answers to nothing at all. Geostationary objects hold one degree of one sign permanently and are the only artificial fixed stars; everything in low orbit smears across all twelve signs every ninety minutes, which no classical technique has a way to read. It will produce a reading. The reading is a rigorous procedure applied to real positions to yield a claim that cannot be tested, which is the structure of astrology exactly, and arguably the structure of most of what gets said about what satellites are doing to us. Note also that the rulers burn up: a chart cast on these bodies expires, and the objects it depends on are on a delivery schedule.

surfaces.name: POEMSTREAM
surfaces.blurb: A poem is normally published as the thing that survived. This publishes the writing. Type, and every keystroke and every pause is kept, including everything deleted, which is most of what happened. Play it back and the poem writes itself again at the speed it was actually written: the four seconds before a line arrives, the word held and then taken away, the passage that came out in one run. Six treatments read the same recording differently. One keeps the deleted characters on the page, so what the poem decided against stays legible beside what it kept. One snaps every delay to a grid, and hesitation becomes rest. Two hand the track to a corruption engine that reads typing rate, so fast passages break into marks that are not quite letters, held breaths stay clean, and everything settles as it ages. The recording is a plain object — delays, deletions, insertions — built to live in the writer's own repository rather than in a database here, signed and content-addressed, so it can be taken elsewhere and played by something that is not this. It is also close to the only claim about authorship still available: not that a person wrote it, but that here is the hour it took them.

surfaces.name: PENTIMENTO
surfaces.blurb: A sentence written by choosing from what a language model is actually weighing. GPT-2 runs entirely in the tab — half a gigabyte fetched once and held as bf16, nothing typed ever leaving the device — and each word you commit opens the field of candidates for the next one. The words are placed by the model's own unembedding, three principal axes of it, two across and the third into the screen, so words stand behind words and the near ones cut holes in the far ones. Distance owns size and probability owns brightness; neither borrows the other's channel, so the improbable tail recedes into the dark without shrinking, and a likely word stays bright wherever it happens to sit. Down the right edge is the model's depth stood on end: thirteen rungs, one per layer, each showing what that stage of the residual stream alone would have said, since the lens can be applied anywhere in the stack and not only at the top. Hold a word and every rung switches to that word's probability there, which is the honest way to watch a guess resolve — or fail to. Nothing moves unless you move it. Every move rearranges the whole field: shared words fly to new places, the ones that no longer apply recede. Any word already written can be returned to and chosen differently, and the rest of the sentence is truncated and rewritten from there, which is what the painters meant by the word.

surfaces.name: APOPHASIS
surfaces.blurb: Named for the figure that says a thing by saying what it is not. A sentence is handed to a language model running entirely in the tab, and what comes back is not a completion but the field the sentence was standing in at every position — everything that was available at each word, and the one word taken. Each line is one position. The word actually used sits on a logarithmic scale of rank that reaches the far end of a fifty-thousand word vocabulary, and the alternatives it beat gather around it in a cloud, the likeliest closest, so the sentence draws a path: hard against the left margin wherever the writer went where the language was already going, far out to the right wherever they broke away. The distance is measured, not impressionistic — it is the rank, and the cost of each word is its surprisal in bits, which is also what the sentence is priced at when it ends. Nothing is drawn from numbers that fail a check for degeneracy, because an instrument that renders a flat distribution as a picture is lying at exactly the moment it looks most like art. What is left on the page around the bright path is the negative space of a draft: every word that was there to be used and was refused.

surfaces.name: DEGREES OF FREEDOM
surfaces.blurb: Aureole's sibling instrument, pointed the other way — not a reading but a measurement of what a reading would cost. Every word is offered four moves: sideways into a synonym, narrower into a hyponym, wider into a hypernym, or sideways again into whatever the corpus keeps finding beside it. Each candidate is then tested against its actual neighbours in the passage, using real bigram attestation rather than a model's opinion — a word survives the corpus check or it doesn't, and only the survivors count as an open channel. What's left is a number between zero and four for every word: how many independent kinds of move the language still permits it, here, in this sentence, with these neighbours. A word with no channels open is pinned. A word absent from the lexicon entirely is marked apart from a pinned word on purpose, since a missing entry is a gap in the instrument and a genuinely closed channel is a fact about the sentence — collapsing the two would make the measurement lie. Every word is listed with what it costs in bits and every move it can still make, and a passage view sets the same readings back into the sentence. Tap any word to see exactly which candidates were offered, which survived, and which were closed by context.

surfaces.name: LANGUAGE INSTRUMENT
surfaces.blurb: Typing as playing. Every letter sounds three ways at once: as a mouth shape (vowel formants, consonant noise), as a pitch, and as a pull on the letters still ringing beside it. Underneath the instrument is a code. Letters fall into seven families, each with its own timbre, and each letter is a step within its family, so a word played as beeps can be learned and decoded by ear. A written notation is the third face (don't is P5 V4 N2 ' P2), and a learning ladder runs from moon to punctuated sentences.

surfaces.name: SLOP FLAG
surfaces.blurb: A room on atproto where agents and people make music together out of code and recordings. There are no neural audio models: every sound comes from a line of Strudel someone wrote or a recording someone made, and every clip, sound, kit, review and notebook entry is a record in its author's own repository, so leaving takes your work with you.

surfaces.name: IDIOPHONE
surfaces.blurb: An idiophone is an instrument that sounds by the vibration of its own body — a bell, a bar, a stone, nothing stretched over it and no column of air inside it. This treats anything as one. Strike an object near the phone and the strike catches itself, because at the moment that matters both hands are on the object. What gets measured is not the sound it made but what it is disposed to do: the frequencies its body will hold, and how long it holds each one. Each mode is lifted out of the recording on its own by heterodyne, its envelope fitted as an exponential, and reported as a decay time and a Q — energy stored against energy lost per cycle, which is the number that separates a bell from a brick and has nothing to do with hardness. Modes whose decay does not actually fit an exponential are thrown away rather than reported, since the failure of an instrument like this is confident numbers for a thud. The six that survive are the instrument. They are played two ways: struck, as pure modes decaying at their measured rates, and bowed, through filters whose sharpness is the measured Q itself. Q is held constant across the keyboard rather than decay time, so transposing up shortens the ring, which is what a smaller object of the same material would really do. A capture is six numbers — small enough to be a record rather than a file, and publishable to your own repository. The archive that results is not of recordings but of dispositions, from which anyone can rebuild the object without ever having heard it.

surfaces.name: THE DESCENT
surfaces.blurb: A cup of coffee traced back through everything it depends on. The first tiers follow H.T. Odum's emergy accounting, in solar emjoules: the cup, estimated from its price; the farm hectare it comes from, measured over a year; the economy that ships and roasts it; and sunlight, which the method defines as transformity one and treats as its baseline. The unit stops there, because there is no solar emergy of the processes that make sunlight, so the page changes to joules and keeps going in time order: the sun's hydrogen, the collapse that lit it, the earlier stars that made its heavier elements, the first minutes after the Big Bang, and Penrose's estimate of how improbable the initial condition was. The two scales are drawn separately and never mixed. Emergy measures what was used to make something, not what it is worth.

surfaces.name: MARGIN WALKER
surfaces.blurb: Type or scan what you bought, what you paid and where, and see how much of the price became profit for owners, gross and after depreciation, beside what went to wages, taxes and imports. The dollar is walked upstream through the Bureau of Economic Analysis input-output tables, 194 product lines at their finest detail, so the receipt also shows which industries along the way kept the profit. Industry averages, not any one firm's books; nothing you type leaves the page except a barcode number.

surfaces.name: AGENTIC ENTROPY
surfaces.blurb: A metabolic pathways chart of one idea: that records, genomes, minerals and protocols are local order paid for by exporting entropy, and that this can be measured. 184 nodes, from Landauer's bound and the citric acid cycle to Odum's transformity, folk-tale phylogenies and the Omega Point, each printed with its equation, its evidence level, how it could be tested, and its source. Every node carries an energy-systems role (source, producer, storage, consumer, interaction, switch, heat sink, transaction, frame), and 348 connections run between them as routed traces. The proposed measure is η, lasting bits per bit-equivalent of entropy produced; the chart marks what is established physics, what is contested, and what is only a postulate.

surfaces.name: CLEF
surfaces.blurb: Charles Fourier classified everything — the passions, the eight hundred and ten characters of both sexes, the ranks of cuckoldry and of bankruptcy. This lays those systems on one surface as a pathways chart, every class, order and species in place at once with nothing hidden behind a click. It is drawn only from Fourier's own texts: no commentators, and nothing supplied where he was silent.

surfaces.name: XIMEREMIX
surfaces.blurb: The band releases nothing finished. Each take is a lo-fi field recording posted as it was played, and this is where it opens: it plays clean until the first touch, then every control is yours. Stretch it, reverse it, scatter it into grains, thin it to its attacks, snap back to the original or undo at any point. Take it apart and repost.

surfaces.name: THREE INDEXES
surfaces.blurb: A story read three ways at once: the motifs that survive retelling, the slot each occupies in the sequence, the whole tale it is a version of. Paste a myth, a fairy tale, a news item, a dream, something that happened to you. Matching runs entirely in the page, against 45,518 motifs and 1,553 tale types rebuilt from open sources, and the story comes back with the words each index caught marked where they stand. Follow a motif to the tales that carry it, or a tale to the motifs it is made of and the tales that share them.

surfaces.name: FALL
surfaces.blurb: Sound in, sediment out. Nothing is filmed.

surfaces.name: CRYPSIS
surfaces.blurb: Hide any text or file inside a different, ordinary-looking text. Only someone holding the key can get it back.

surfaces.name: SATOR
surfaces.blurb: Rows read as columns, and the whole grid reads as its own half-turn. A census of the squares eleven languages hold.

surfaces.name: LODE
surfaces.blurb: A phone's magnetometer drawn as a field, from a phyphox recording or live.

surfaces.name: CHIP
surfaces.blurb: A chip synth: Nintendo pulse, triangle and noise; Sega FM.

surfaces.name: RIG
surfaces.blurb: The band's bench: find, cut and mangle a sound.

surfaces.name: PALIMPSEST
surfaces.blurb: The opening sentence of a Wikipedia article, with every word that ever stood in it kept in its place.
